lessons.title: Sincerity: the reason behind the deed
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith teach about the reason behind a deed.

steps.title: Why start with the reason
body: Two people can do the same deed. One does it for Allah. The other does it to be seen. The deed looks the same from outside. Ikhlas (sincerity) is about the reason behind it.
This lesson teaches what Allah and His Messenger ﷺ said about the reason, in four short texts.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah commanded
body: Allah says: “And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion” (98:5).
Sincerity is part of what we were commanded to do. It is not an extra.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The hadith of intentions
body: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «The reward of deeds depends upon the intentions, and every person will get the reward according to what he has intended. So whoever emigrated for worldly benefits or for a woman to marry, his emigration was for what he emigrated for»” (Bukhari 1).
Two men made the same journey. Their reward was not the same, because the reason was not the same.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Three people judged first
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that the first people judged on the Day of Judgment will be a man who died as a martyr, a man who learned and taught knowledge and recited the Qur’an, and a man whom Allah had made rich. Each will list the blessings he enjoyed, and each will say what he did with them (Muslim 1905).

To each Allah will say: you lied. The fighter fought so that it would be said he was brave. The scholar studied so that it would be said he was a scholar and a reciter. The rich man gave so that it would be said he was generous. And it was said. Orders are passed and each is dragged on his face into the Fire (Muslim 1905).
This hadith is serious. It teaches us to be afraid of showing off (riya), and to keep asking why we do what we do.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah says about deeds done for others
body: The Prophet ﷺ reported that Allah the Most High said: “I am the One, Who does not stand in need of a partner. If anyone does anything in which he associates anyone else with Me, I shall abandon him with the one whom he associates with Allah” (Muslim 2985).
This is a hadith qudsi: the words are the Prophet’s ﷺ report of what Allah said.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The line about hadith qudsi is a general description. Please confirm the wording of Muslim 2985 as quoted.

steps.title: What sincerity is not
body: It does not mean no one can ever see your good deed. The hadith of the three speaks about a person who did a thing for the praise.
Nor does it mean you must be sure of your own sincerity. The scholars warn us to fear for it. We ask Allah to accept, and we keep checking our reasons.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: These two notes are the usual teaching of scholars and are drawn from Muslim 1905 and not stated in it. Please confirm.

steps.title: A way to check the reason
body: Before a deed, ask: why am I doing this? Is it for Allah? Would I still do it if no one knew?
After a deed, ask Allah to accept it, and do not tell it to people unless there is a good reason.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Renewing your intention

steps.text: Pause before the deed.
steps.detail: Bukhari 1: the reward follows the intention.

steps.text: Say in your heart: this is for Allah.
Do the deed.
If a thought of praise comes, push it away and go on.
Ask Allah to accept it.

steps.intro: A short plan for any deed.
mistakes: Waiting for a perfect heart before acting.
Stopping a good deed because you feel you are showing off.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps are general guidance. The idea of not stopping a good deed for fear of riya is a common teaching of scholars; please confirm.

lessons.title: Patience: holding on with Allah
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith say about patience and how to practise it.

steps.title: Patience is active
body: Sabr (patience) is often heard as “put up with it”. In the texts it is firmer: holding yourself back from what Allah dislikes, keeping on with what He loves, and staying with Him through a hard time.
This lesson takes the main texts on patience and a few ways to practise it.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The three-part description of sabr is the common teaching of scholars, and is not a quotation. Please confirm or reword.

steps.title: Help through patience
body: Allah says: “And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah]” (2:45).
Patience and prayer are the two tools. Neither is easy. Both are given to those who bow to Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The test and the words
body: Allah says: “And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, «Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return»” (2:155-156).
The test is promised. The good news is for those who are patient and turn to Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the patient say
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught these words for a calamity, as Umm Salama reported (Muslim 918). They are also the words of the verse above (2:156).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Yaqub’s patience
body: When Yaqub lost his son, he said: “I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know” (12:86). He told his sons to go and look for Yusuf and not to despair of relief from Allah (12:87).
He cried, and he kept his hope. Patience does not mean you do not feel. It means you take the feeling to Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The first stroke
body: The Prophet ﷺ passed a woman crying at a grave. He told her to fear Allah and be patient. She did not know him and answered sharply. When she knew who it was, she came to his door and said she had not known him. He said that real patience is at the first stroke (Bukhari 1283).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Patience can be built
body: Abu Said al-Khudri reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever remains patient, Allah will make him patient. Nobody can be given a blessing better and greater than patience” (Bukhari 1469).
So you do not have to wait until you are patient. You try, and Allah helps.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Good in every case
body: Suhayb reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Strange are the ways of a believer, for there is good in every affair of his. If he has an occasion to feel delight, he thanks Allah, and there is good for him in it. If he gets into trouble and endures it patiently, there is good for him in it” (Muslim 2999).
Thanks in ease and patience in hardship both bring good.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Practising patience

steps.text: Name the hard thing out loud to yourself.
Say the words of 2:156.
Hold your tongue and your hands in the first moment.
Pray two rakahs and ask Allah for help.
Keep doing what you must do that day.
Tell Allah your grief, as Yaqub did.

steps.intro: A short plan for a hard day.
mistakes: Complaining about Allah instead of to Him.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps combine texts with general guidance. Please confirm.

steps.prompt: Put these in order.

lessons.title: Gratitude: the promise of increase
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith say about gratitude and how to practise it.

steps.title: Gratitude is more than a word
body: Shukr (gratitude) has three parts: the heart knows the blessing is from Allah, the tongue says so, and the body uses the blessing in a way Allah likes.
This lesson takes the texts on gratitude, then gives you short practices.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The three-part description of shukr is the common teaching of scholars and is not a quotation. Please confirm.

steps.title: What Allah promised
body: Allah says: “And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, «If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe»” (14:7).
The promise is increase for the grateful. The warning is for those who deny blessings.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The Prophet ﷺ in prayer
body: Al-Mughirah reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to stand in prayer until his feet swelled. He was asked why he did this, and he said: “Should I not be a thankful slave?” (Bukhari 1130).
He did not pray for himself alone. He prayed as thanks. Even those who are forgiven give thanks.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Gratitude in ease
body: Suhayb reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that a believer, if he has an occasion to feel delight, thanks Allah, and there is good for him in it (Muslim 2999).
Ease is a test of gratitude, as hardship is a test of patience.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Look at those below you
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Look at those who stand at a lower level than you, and do not look at those who stand at a higher level than you, for that is better-suited that you do not disparage Allah’s favors” (Muslim 2963).
Comparing upward makes us feel poor. Looking at those with less keeps the blessing in view.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: True wealth
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Wealth is not in having many possessions, but rather true wealth is feeling sufficiency in the soul” (Bukhari 6446).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Thanking people
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “He who does not thank the people is not thankful to Allah” (Abu Dawud 4811, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
So gratitude to Allah includes saying thank you to those who helped you.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 4811, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: Thanks after food
steps.note: These are the words the Prophet ﷺ said when his food was lifted (Bukhari 5458). It is one way to give thanks for something we receive every day.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Practising gratitude

steps.text: Name three blessings you did not earn.
Say alhamdulillah for each, out loud.
Thank one person by name.
steps.detail: Abu Dawud 4811, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai.

Look at someone with less before you complain.

mistakes: Thanking Allah only when things go well.
Thanking Allah but not the people who helped.

steps.review: The steps combine texts and general guidance. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Truthfulness: the road and the story of Kab
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ said about truth and lies, and the story of Kab ibn Malik.

steps.title: Where the truth leads
body: A small lie seems cheap. The Prophet ﷺ taught that speech shapes the person who speaks. This lesson takes his words and one true story of a man who chose the truth when a lie would have been easier.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The road of truth and the road of lies
body: Abdullah ibn Masud reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. And a man keeps on telling the truth until he becomes a truthful person. Falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire, and a man may keep on telling lies till he is written before Allah a liar” (Bukhari 6094).
Habits are built word by word. Both roads start with a small step.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A sign of hypocrisy
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: whenever he speaks, he tells a lie; whenever he promises, he breaks it; if you trust him, he proves dishonest” (Bukhari 33).
The hadith names speech first. The three signs are about habit and not about one slip.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The note that these are signs of habit and not of one slip is the usual teaching of scholars. Please confirm.

steps.title: Be with the truthful
body: Allah says: “O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true” (9:119).
The verse asks for two things: fear of Allah, and company with the truthful.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Kab ibn Malik stays behind
body: Kab ibn Malik stayed behind from the expedition to Tabuk without an excuse. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, Kab said he thought up false excuses, and then he gave them up. He knew he could never come out of this by a false statement, so he decided firmly to speak the truth (Bukhari 4418).

He said to the Prophet ﷺ: “If I tell you a lie to seek your favour, Allah would surely make you angry with me soon. If I tell you the truth, though you will be angry, I hope for Allah’s forgiveness. By Allah, there was no excuse for me.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “As for this man, he has told the truth. So get up until Allah decides your case” (Bukhari 4418).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The wait and the verse
body: Kab and two others waited a long time for a decision. At the end, Allah revealed the verses that forgave the three (9:118), followed by the command to be with the truthful (9:119). Kab said that, after guiding him to Islam, Allah never gave him a greater blessing than his not lying to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (Bukhari 4418).
The truth cost him a hard time. It also saved him.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What about hard cases?
body: Some situations make people ask whether a lie is ever allowed, such as to protect a life or to make peace. Scholars discuss these cases using other texts, and the schools do not give the same answer in every detail.
This lesson does not rule on them. Ask a scholar of your school. For ordinary life the rule is plain: tell the truth.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Scholars of the four schools (not cited here)
steps.review: The note that the schools differ on hard cases is general. Please confirm or give the schools.

steps.title: Practising truthfulness

steps.text: Pick one small place where you shade the truth (excuses, “on my way”, “I read it”).
Stop and say the plain thing instead.
Keep your promises, or say early that you cannot.
Return what is entrusted to you.
Spend time with people who tell the truth.

steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps combine texts with general guidance. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Anger: control and refuge
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ said about anger, the words to say, and a short plan to cool down.

steps.title: Anger is a fire
body: Anger is a feeling every person has. The texts do not ask us to feel nothing. They ask us to control what we do with it.
This lesson gives you the words of the Prophet ﷺ, one phrase to say, and steps to cool down.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Who is strong
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The strong is not the one who overcomes the people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger” (Bukhari 6114).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Advise me
body: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Advise me.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not become angry.” The man asked again and again, and each time the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not become angry” (Bukhari 6116).
The man asked for advice, and this was the advice he was given, over and over.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah loves
body: Allah describes the doers of good as those “who spend [in the cause of Allah] during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good” (3:134).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The man whose face turned red
body: Sulayman ibn Surad said that he was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when two men abused each other. The face of one turned red and his veins swelled. The Prophet ﷺ said: “I know a word, which if he says it, what he feels will go away. If he said: «I seek refuge with Allah from Satan», what he feels would go away” (Bukhari 3282).
The people told the man what the Prophet ﷺ had said. He answered: “Am I mad?” (Bukhari 3282). He refused, and we are not told he calmed down.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The words to say
steps.note: These are the words the Prophet ﷺ said would take away the anger. Say them quietly, in your heart or aloud, as soon as you feel it rise.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Change your position
body: Abu Dharr reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you becomes angry while standing, he should sit down. If the anger leaves him, well and good; otherwise he should lie down” (Abu Dawud 4782, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
A small physical change can lower the heat.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 4782, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: Is all anger wrong?
body: The hadith does not ask us to stop feeling anger. It asks us to control ourselves in it. Anger for the sake of Allah, for example at injustice, is a different matter, and scholars discuss when it is right to act on it.
This lesson is about personal anger: at family, friends and colleagues.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The note on righteous anger is general teaching and not a quotation. Please confirm.

steps.title: When you feel it rise

steps.text: Stop speaking.
Say: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan.
If you are standing, sit down. If still angry, lie down.

steps.text: Make wudu if you can.
steps.detail: General guidance; it is often taught but the text is not cited here.

steps.text: Come back to the matter when it has cooled.

mistakes: Keeping it in and growing a grudge.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The wudu step is a common teaching and is not cited. Please confirm or remove.

lessons.title: Envy: the second look
lessons.intro: Learn the difference between envy and ghibtah, and a cure taken from the texts.

steps.title: The second look
body: Envy (hasad) is wishing that a blessing leave another person. It is different from wishing you had the same good. The first is blamed in the texts. This lesson separates the two, and gives a cure.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The definition of hasad as wishing a blessing leave another is the usual scholarly definition and is not a quotation. Please confirm.

steps.title: Do not wish for what Allah gave others
body: Allah says: “And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of his bounty” (4:32).
The way out is in the last words: ask Allah of His bounty.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Seeking refuge from the envier
body: Allah teaches us to seek refuge “from the evil of an envier when he envies” (113:5).
So envy is a real harm, and Allah gives us a way to ask for protection from it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the Prophet ﷺ forbade
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the worst of false tales. Do not look for others’ faults, do not spy, do not be jealous of one another, do not desert one another, and do not hate one another. O servants of Allah! Be brothers” (Bukhari 6064).
Envy is put next to spying, desertion and hatred, the things that break brotherhood.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The good kind: wanting the same
body: Abdullah ibn Masud reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not wish to be like anyone except in two cases: a person to whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it righteously, and one to whom Allah has given wisdom and he acts according to it and teaches it to others” (Bukhari 73).
Wishing to do good as others do, without wishing them to lose it, is allowed. Scholars call it ghibtah.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The term ghibtah is the usual scholarly name for this and is not in the hadith. Please confirm.

steps.title: The cure: pray for them
body: The cure for envy is to do the opposite: make dua for the person, by name. A believer is asked to love for his brother what he loves for himself. Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “None of you will have faith till he wishes for his brother what he likes for himself” (Bukhari 13).
Praying for good for them starts to move the heart.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A report we do not rely on
body: A widely quoted saying says that envy eats good deeds as fire eats wood. Its chain is graded weak, so we do not teach it as a hadith. The teaching on envy above does not depend on it.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: This refers to a weak report in Abu Dawud which the old course text cited with the grade weak. No number is cited here. Please confirm.

steps.text: Admit it to yourself, plainly.
Do not speak against the person.
Make dua for them by name.
Ask Allah for your own good.
Seek refuge from the harm of envy.
Go and congratulate them.

lessons.title: Arrogance: the false height
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ said pride is, the warnings, and how he showed humility.

steps.title: The false height
body: Arrogance (kibr) makes a person feel above others and above the truth. It was the first sin of Iblis. This lesson gives the definition the Prophet ﷺ gave, the warnings, and the humility he showed.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What arrogance is
body: Abdullah ibn Masud reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “He who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of pride shall not enter Paradise.” A man said: “A person loves that his dress should be fine and his shoes should be fine.” He said: “Allah is Graceful and He loves grace. Pride is disdaining the truth and contempt for the people” (Muslim 91).
So fine clothes are not pride. Pride is refusing the truth and looking down on people.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The first arrogance
body: When Allah asked Iblis what prevented him from prostrating, he said: «I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay» (7:12).
Allah said: “Descend from Paradise, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein” (7:13). Arrogance began with comparing: I am better than him.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: How the servants of the Merciful walk
body: Allah says: “And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace” (25:63).
He also says: “And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height” (17:37).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A warning
body: Haritha ibn Wahb reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “May I tell you of the people of Paradise? Every weak and poor obscure person whom people look down upon, but whose oath Allah fulfils. And may I inform you of the people of the Fire? They are all the violent, arrogant and stubborn” (Bukhari 4918).
The people looked down on are the ones he named first.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: How he behaved
body: Anas ibn Malik said: “Any of the female slaves of Madinah could take hold of the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and take him wherever she wished” (Bukhari 6072).
The leader of the community let anyone stop him and ask for help.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Where it hides
body: Pride can hide in how we treat those who serve us, in refusing advice, and in not saying sorry. These are examples that scholars use from Muslim 91; they are not cited as sayings of the Prophet ﷺ.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The three places named are general illustrations and not quoted. Please confirm.

steps.title: Practising humility

steps.text: Say sorry first when you are wrong.
Accept advice, even from someone younger.
Do a small service that is below your rank.
Reply to a rude word with peace.
Do one good deed that nobody sees.

steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps combine texts and general guidance. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Despair: the door that is open
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith say to the person who thinks it is too late.

steps.title: The closed door that is not closed
body: Despair says: it is too late for me. The Qur’an and the Prophet ﷺ answer this directly. This lesson gives Allah’s words, the hadith of the servant who sinned and came back, and what to do tonight.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Allah calls the ones who sinned
body: Allah says: “Say, «O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful»” (39:53).
The call is to servants who have sinned. It does not say “do not sin”. It says: do not give up on mercy.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Who despairs?
body: Yaqub told his sons: “O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people” (12:87).
Ibrahim, when told of good news in old age, said: “And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?” (15:56).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The servant who sinned again and again
body: The Prophet ﷺ reported that his Lord said: a servant sinned and said: “O Allah, forgive me my sin.” Allah said: “My servant has sinned and then realised that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes to account for them.” He sinned again and said the same, and Allah said the same. Then Allah said: “O servant, do what you like. I have granted you forgiveness” (Muslim 2758).
The scholars explain the last words as meaning that as long as the servant keeps coming back in repentance, Allah keeps forgiving. They do not mean that sin is allowed.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The scholarly explanation of “do what you like” is given in general terms and is not cited to a named scholar. Please confirm and name the source.

steps.title: As My servant thinks of Me
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, stated: “I am near to the thought of My servant as he thinks about Me, and I am with him as he remembers Me” (Muslim 2675).
Think well of Allah, as you ask Him.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Allah loves those who return
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “By Him in Whose Hand is my life, if you were not to commit sin, Allah would sweep you out of existence and replace you by people who would commit sin and seek forgiveness from Allah, and He would pardon them” (Muslim 2749).
This does not tell us to sin. It tells us that the need to turn back to Allah is part of being human, and that He loves that return.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The sentence that it does not tell us to sin is an explanation and not a quotation. Please confirm.

steps.title: Two sides, not one
body: Hope without fear can lead to carelessness. Fear without hope leads to despair. The scholars of Islam ask us to hold both.
This lesson is about the second: do not fall into despair.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The teaching on hope and fear is the common teaching of scholars. Please confirm.

steps.title: Coming back tonight

steps.text: Stop the sin if it is ongoing.
Say plainly to Allah what you did.
Ask: O Allah, forgive me.
Think well of Allah.
Do a good deed after it.
If you have wronged a person, put it right with them.

steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps combine texts and general guidance on tawbah. Please confirm.

lessons.title: The tongue: your daily ledger
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ said about speech, and a filter to use before you speak.

steps.title: The small muscle
body: The tongue is small, and the Prophet ﷺ spoke of it more than of almost any other part of the body. This lesson takes four of his sayings and two verses, and gives a daily check.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Speak good or be silent
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbour. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should talk what is good or keep quiet” (Bukhari 6018).
Silence is allowed. Harm is not.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The guarantee
body: Sahl ibn Sad reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever can guarantee what is between his two jaw-bones and what is between his two legs, I guarantee Paradise for him” (Bukhari 6474).
The tongue and the private parts are the two things named.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A word you do not think about
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “A slave may utter a word which pleases Allah without giving it much importance, and because of that Allah will raise him to degrees. A slave may utter a word which displeases Allah without thinking of its gravity, and because of that he will be thrown into the Fire” (Bukhari 6478).
One careless word can go either way. Both words were spoken without much thought, so we should think.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What backbiting is
body: The Prophet ﷺ asked: “Do you know what backbiting is?” The Companions said Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “Your talking about your brother in a manner which he does not like.” It was said: “What if that failing is in my brother?” He said: “If that failing is found in him, you have backbitten him. If it is not in him, it is slander” (Muslim 2589).
So the test is not whether it is true. The test is whether he would dislike it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah says
body: Allah says: “O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it” (49:12).
In the verse before it, Allah forbids ridiculing others and calling each other by offensive nicknames (49:11).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Are there exceptions?
body: Scholars list a few cases where speaking of a person’s fault is allowed, such as to seek justice from a judge, to warn someone of a real harm, or to ask a scholar for a ruling. The schools agree on the principle and differ on some details.
This lesson does not list them in full. If you think your case is one of them, ask a scholar of your school.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Scholars of the four schools (not cited here)

lessons.title: Forgiveness: releasing the debt
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith teach about pardon, and the story of Abu Bakr and Mistah.

steps.title: Letting someone go free
body: When someone wrongs you, you hold a debt in your heart. Forgiveness is releasing that debt. The texts show it is not weakness, and that it is not the same as pretending nothing happened.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The framing of forgiveness as releasing a debt is a teaching image and not a quotation. Please confirm.

steps.title: Justice is allowed; pardon is better
body: Allah says: “And the retribution for an evil act is an evil one like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is [due] from Allah. Indeed, He does not like wrongdoers” (42:40).
You may seek a fair answer to a wrong. Pardon with reconciliation has a reward from Allah himself.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Those Allah loves
body: Allah describes the doers of good as those “who spend during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good” (3:134).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Forgiving raises you
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Charity does not decrease wealth, no one forgives another except that Allah increases his honour, and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah except that Allah raises his status” (Muslim 2588).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Abu Bakr and Mistah
body: In the slander against Aisha, Mistah ibn Uthathah, a poor relative whom Abu Bakr supported, was among those who spread it (Bukhari 4141). Abu Bakr swore he would stop helping him.

Then Allah revealed: “And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful” (24:22).
Abu Bakr said: “Yes, by Allah, I would like that Allah forgive me.” He went on giving Mistah what he used to give (Bukhari 4141).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Keeping ties with those who cut you
body: Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The one who keeps ties is not the one who repays the good done to him by relatives, but the one who keeps good relations with relatives who have cut the tie with him” (Bukhari 5991).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What forgiveness is not
body: It is not saying the wrong was right. It is not staying in danger. It does not cancel a legal right where a judge or a victim has a right in law, and scholars discuss these cases. If you are being abused, forgiveness in the heart does not mean you must stay.
For a real case, ask a scholar of your school.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: These limits are general teaching and are not cited to a named text. Please confirm.

steps.title: Releasing a debt

steps.text: Name what was done to you.
Decide whether you seek your right or pardon, as 42:40 allows both.
If you choose to pardon, say it to Allah.
Make a dua for them.
If it is safe, do them a small kindness.

mistakes: Saying you forgive and then bringing it up again.
Staying near someone who is harming you.

lessons.title: Kindness: the Prophet at home
lessons.intro: Learn how the Prophet ﷺ was kind at home and in the mosque, and what Allah says of gentleness.

steps.title: Kindness at home and outside
body: Rifq (gentleness, kindness) is a way of doing things: softly, with ease. The Prophet ﷺ was kind in his house, in the mosque and in public. This lesson gives three scenes and two sayings.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What he did at home
body: Al-Aswad asked Aisha: “What did the Prophet ﷺ use to do in his house?” She replied: “He used to keep himself busy serving his family, and when it was the time for prayer he would go for it” (Bukhari 676).
The man everyone looked to for guidance spent his time at home helping.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The man in the mosque
body: A bedouin urinated in the mosque and the people ran to beat him. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not interrupt his urination.” Then he asked for water and had it poured over the place (Bukhari 6025).
In another narration he said: “You have been sent to make things easy, and not to make them difficult” (Bukhari 220).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Allah loves kindness
body: Aisha reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Aisha, verily Allah is kind and He loves kindness, and He confers upon kindness what He does not confer upon severity, nor upon anything besides it” (Muslim 2593).
Jarir reported that he said: “He who is deprived of tender feelings is in fact deprived of good” (Muslim 2592).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah said to the Prophet ﷺ
body: Allah says: “So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you” (3:159).
Harshness drives people away. Gentleness brings them near.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Repel evil with better
body: Allah says: “And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend” (41:34).
The next verse says that none is granted this except those who are patient (41:35).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Kind does not mean weak
body: Gentleness does not mean saying yes to everything, or letting wrong go on. The Prophet ﷺ stopped the people from beating the man, and he also had the place cleaned. Both were done.
The scholars teach that kindness and firmness belong together; this lesson focuses on kindness.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The sentence on scholars teaching kindness and firmness together is a general summary. Please confirm or cite.

steps.title: A day of small kindnesses

steps.text: Do one job at home before you are asked.
When someone gets it wrong, correct them gently and help fix it.
Answer a harsh word with a soft one.
Make things easy for others.
End the day by thanking one person.

mistakes: Being kind to guests and harsh at home.

lessons.title: Brotherhood: the whole body
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ taught about the bond between believers.

steps.title: One body
body: The believers are not a crowd of separate people. The Prophet ﷺ compared them to one body. This lesson gives that picture, what a brother or sister owes, and what makes it real.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The body
body: Al-Numan ibn Bashir reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You see the believers in their mercy among themselves, their love among themselves and their kindness, like one body: if any part of the body is not well, the whole body shares the sleeplessness and fever with it” (Bukhari 6011).
In Muslim 2586 the same picture is given in the words: “when any limb of it aches, the whole body aches, because of sleeplessness and fever”.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The verse
body: Allah says: “The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy” (49:10).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What a brother owes
body: Abdullah ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim is the brother of another Muslim, so he should not oppress him, nor hand him over to an oppressor. Whoever fulfilled the needs of his brother, Allah will fulfil his needs. Whoever brought his brother out of a discomfort, Allah will bring him out of the discomforts of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever screened a Muslim, Allah will screen him on the Day of Resurrection” (Bukhari 2442).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Love for your brother what you love for yourself
body: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “None of you will have faith till he wishes for his brother what he likes for himself” (Bukhari 13).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What breaks it
body: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not nurse grudges, do not nurse aversion or enmity, and be fellow-brothers and servants of Allah. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He neither oppresses him, nor humiliates him, nor looks down upon him. Piety is here” and he pointed to his chest three times (Muslim 2564).
The same hadith says: “Allah does not look to your bodies nor to your faces, but He looks to your hearts” (Muslim 2564).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Who is a brother here?
body: The texts above speak of the brotherhood of believers. The Qur’an and Sunnah also command justice and kindness to people who are not Muslim (for example, 60:8). This lesson is about the bond between believers.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The reference to 60:8 is as a pointer only and not quoted here. Please confirm.

steps.title: Checking on a brother or sister

steps.text: Think of one person you have not spoken to this month.
Send a message or call.
Ask what they need, and do it if you can.
Cover a fault of theirs instead of telling others.
Make dua for them.

mistakes: Waiting for them to call first.
Offering help you do not mean.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The steps combine texts and general guidance. Please confirm.
